# Go Gotchas

> Known Go patterns that cause silent failures or hard-to-debug errors.

## Entries

- [Resetting a sync.Once by reassigning it is fatal, not just racy](sync-once-reset.md): `once = sync.Once{}` to invalidate a cache hands an in-flight `Do()` a zeroed mutex, killing the process with `fatal error: sync: unlock of unlocked mutex`; the stack names the victim goroutine, not the reassigning one, and `go vet` stays clean. HIGH.
- [A `_darwin`/`_windows` filename silently makes a test file unrunnable, and CI may run that GOOS nowhere](goos-filename-suffix-makes-tests-unrunnable.md): Go takes an implicit build constraint from the filename and strips `_test` first, so `x_darwin_test.go` is darwin-only with no tag involved -- and an explicit `//go:build` is ANDed, not substituted, so `//go:build linux` on `x_darwin.go` builds nowhere. Nothing reports the absence: `go test ./...` says ok, `GOOS=darwin go vet` is clean, coverage shows no gap, and a test that has never run is indistinguishable from one that passes. It closes when CI builds the macOS artifact on macos-latest but runs the Go test job on ubuntu/windows -- then every `_darwin_test.go` executes on no machine ever while reading as coverage. Seen live: 223 lines of macOS parsing tests that had never executed, which found a real defect the first time they ran. Keep the platform file to the syscall boundary, put pure logic in an un-suffixed file, and prove it with `go test -run <name> -v` (before the fix: "no tests to run"). HIGH.
- [A test that asserts properties of a *sequence* proves nothing when the fixture makes one element](sequence-assertions-vacuous-on-one-element.md): "element N+1 follows element N" assertions -- monotonic counters, cumulative offsets, non-overlapping ranges -- are vacuously true over a collection of one, so the loop body never runs and the test reports PASS. The assertions are correct; the fixture is wrong, and a green run cannot tell the two apart. Seen live: six fMP4 muxer tests on fragment sequence numbers, decode times and data offsets all held against a one-keyframe stream (which produces exactly one fragment) and hid a writer that never advanced a fragment's base decode time. Coverage does not help -- the lines all execute. Guard arity in the shared helper (`t.Fatalf` when `len < 2`), and prove each invariant by mutating the line and confirming a *named* test fails. HIGH.
- [`stsd` and `dref` are ISO-BMFF full boxes, so a generic box walker cannot descend into them](stsd-dref-are-full-boxes-not-containers.md): Both hold child boxes and so look like containers, but their payload starts with version|flags|entry_count -- recursing at offset 0 reads those eight bytes as a size and type, so the walk fails with an impossible size or succeeds against garbage. Symptom is a test that cannot find `avc1` although the writer emitted it, which sends you debugging the muxer instead of the reader. Skip 8 bytes for stsd/dref; `avcC` is not reachable by walking at all (it sits 78 bytes into avc1's fixed-width VisualSampleEntry fields). Make the walker return an error rather than calling t.Fatalf, so it can be self-tested against a box that lies about its size. MEDIUM.
- [A Wails binding serializes with encoding/json, so the webview sees struct tags, not Go field names](wails-binding-json-tags.md): a binding returning a Go struct marshals it with encoding/json, so the webview receives its struct TAGS -- `urls`, not `URLs`. Write the TypeScript type from the Go source and every field reads `undefined`; the `.filter()` or `?? default` that almost always follows a binding call then drops EVERY entry and hands back a well-formed empty collection rather than an error, and a hand-written binding type declaring the wrong spelling as optional makes it type-check. Seen live: a remote-desktop viewer read `server.URLs` off []ICEServerConfig and built every RTCPeerConnection with `iceServers: []` -- which still negotiates, still trickles host candidates, and fails ~15s later as `failed`, indistinguishable from a tenant with no relay configured. It connects on a flat LAN, so it reads as "certain machines are unreachable" and sends you to the customer's firewall. Read the struct tags before writing the TS type, accept both spellings, and assert the COUNT survives the mapping -- "some entries came through" reads as success until the one that would have connected is the one dropped. HIGH.
- [cgo silently refuses pkg-config flags it does not recognise, and the error names the flag rather than the fix](cgo-pkgconfig-flag-allowlist.md): cgo runs every compiler and linker flag through a fixed allowlist (`cmd/go/internal/work/security.go`) to stop a malicious `.pc` file injecting `-fplugin=` or `@file` at build time -- and ordinary flags from well-known libraries are not on it. libpipewire emits `-fno-strict-overflow`, so `#cgo pkg-config: libpipewire-0.3` fails with "invalid flag in pkg-config --cflags". The message names a flag you never wrote (it came from the library's `.pc`), so grepping your own source finds nothing; it reads as a missing `-dev` package or a bad `PKG_CONFIG_PATH`, both of which are fine; and it only appears once something actually compiles the cgo package, so the editor and `gopls` stay quiet until CI. Fix is `CGO_CFLAGS_ALLOW` (a REGEX, not a list) set on every invocation that compiles -- build, vet, test, and wrappers like `wails build` -- which is why setting it in one place and missing the others is the usual second round. Keep the pattern narrow: `.*` restores the build and removes the protection. Related trap in the same preamble: a `//` comment block immediately above `/* ... */ import "C"` is absorbed into the C source and fails as C syntax errors quoting your own prose. MEDIUM.
- [A pion track with an empty SDPFmtpLine can never exact-match, so it binds to the offerer's first H.264](pion-h264-empty-fmtp.md): `RTPCodecCapability{MimeType: MimeTypeH264}` with no fmtp reads as "defaults are fine" and is not. `h264FMTP.Match` returns false whenever `packetization-mode` is missing on either side, so the exact pass in `codecParametersFuzzySearch` cannot ever fire and every session falls through to the partial pass, which returns the FIRST H.264 in the negotiated list. As the answerer that ordering is the browser's, varying by version, platform and hardware, so landing on a `packetization-mode=0` entry gives a connected track whose FU-A fragments the decoder discards: ICE connected, bytesReceived climbing, framesDecoded stuck at 0, black forever, no error either side. It also takes the mouse with it, because a never-decoded video has videoWidth 0 and click mapping refuses a zero-sized picture, so it reads as two unrelated bugs. Register only the variants you can produce (both 42001f AND 42e01f, since profileLevelIDMatches compares profile_iop), remember a hand-built MediaEngine gets no interceptors, and declare the track's fmtp. HIGH.
